newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo admits much larger copper trading loss. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo admits much larger copper trading loss. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]

text.p: Sumitomo Corp. admitted on Thursday that losses from a massive copper trading scandal had soared to $2.6 billion from the $1.8 billion it originally estimated.

The statement came in a revision of the trading group's earnings forecast. The company said that it revised its group net forecast for 1996-97 to show a loss of 147 billion yen ($1.34 billion) from a profit of 24 billion yen ($220 million).
The company also announced that it would ask prosecutors to bring criminal charges against the man it said is behind the scandal, fired copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
(Corrects to make clear Sumitomo is not suing Hamanaka but asking for criminal charges to be brought against him).
The trade house announced on June 13 that it had suffered the huge losses from unauthorised copper trades.
It also said that despite the huge loss it would maintain its 1996/97 dividend at eight yen (7.3 cents).

Traders and financial analysts had questioned Sumitomo's previous loss estimate, saying it appeared to be much too low given the company's huge exposure in the market and the sharp fall in copper prices since the scandal broke.
